common_name: Garvinea Series Gerbera Daisy (Cold-Hardier Weatherproof Perennial Gerbera)

planting.note: Start indoors 8-10 weeks before last frost and transplant out after hardening off into fertile, well-drained soil in full sun; Garvinea was bred specifically for improved cold tolerance and weather resistance over florist-type gerbera.

directions: Start indoors 8-10 weeks before last frost and transplant out after hardening off into fertile, well-drained soil in full sun. Garvinea bears an abundance of smaller, daisy-like flowers in bright reds, oranges, yellows, pinks, and whites over a low rosette of deep green foliage, bred to be noticeably more weatherproof and cold-tolerant than standard florist gerbera cultivars, holding up better to rain and wind without the flowers collapsing. Its improved hardiness allows it to survive as a genuine garden perennial in warmer zones rather than requiring replacement each year like more tender gerbera types. Water at the base rather than overhead to reduce crown rot, deadhead spent flowers to encourage continued bloom, and treat as an annual in zones colder than its hardy range.

common_name: Festival Series Gerbera Daisy (Compact Patio Gerbera)

planting.note: Start indoors 8-10 weeks before last frost and transplant out after hardening off into fertile, well-drained soil in full sun; Festival is a compact series bred for uniform pot and patio-container production.

directions: Start indoors 8-10 weeks before last frost and transplant out after hardening off into fertile, well-drained soil in full sun. Festival bears large, brightly colored, daisy-like flowers in a wide range of colors on an especially compact, uniform, low-growing plant bred specifically for potted and patio-container production, staying tidy and proportional in a small pot rather than sprawling. Its compact habit and heavy, continuous bloom have made it a popular choice for retail flowering pot plants as well as garden borders. Water at the base rather than overhead to reduce crown rot, deadhead spent flowers to encourage continued bloom, and treat as an annual in zones colder than 8 or a short-lived perennial in warmer climates.

common_name: Everlast Series Gerbera Daisy (Exceptionally Weather-Tolerant Garden Gerbera)

planting.note: Start indoors 8-10 weeks before last frost and transplant out after hardening off into fertile, well-drained soil in full sun; Everlast was bred for exceptional resistance to rain and wind damage compared with standard gerbera.

directions: Start indoors 8-10 weeks before last frost and transplant out after hardening off into fertile, well-drained soil in full sun. Everlast bears large, brightly colored, daisy-like flowers on sturdy stems above a compact rosette of deep green foliage, bred for exceptional durability against rain, wind, and heat that can knock down or fade the blooms of less weather-tolerant gerbera cultivars. Its strong garden performance through difficult summer weather has made it a reliable choice for beds and containers that see more exposure than a sheltered patio. Water at the base rather than overhead to reduce crown rot, deadhead spent flowers to encourage continued bloom, and treat as an annual in zones colder than 8 or a short-lived perennial in warmer climates.

common_name: Jaguar Series Gerbera Daisy (Large-Flowered Strong-Stemmed Garden Gerbera)

planting.note: Start indoors 8-10 weeks before last frost and transplant out after hardening off into fertile, well-drained soil in full sun; Jaguar is bred for unusually large flowers on strong, upright stems.

directions: Start indoors 8-10 weeks before last frost and transplant out after hardening off into fertile, well-drained soil in full sun. Jaguar bears unusually large, vividly colored, daisy-like flowers on strong, upright stems that hold the heavy blooms well above the foliage without flopping, a bolder scale than many compact patio gerbera series. Its combination of large flower size and sturdy stems makes it useful both for garden beds and as a cut flower, since the strong stems hold up well once cut for a vase. Water at the base rather than overhead to reduce crown rot, deadhead spent flowers to encourage continued bloom, and treat as an annual in zones colder than 8 or a short-lived perennial in warmer climates.
